Appendix B.2 
Backesting of $\zeta$ values using three databases: KLEMS, NBER CES, and STAN.

# Notes

Errors are expressed in base points (1bp= 0.01 log percentage point).


```{r}
library(here)
source(here("0_set_up.R"))
source("2.0 functions_hindcasting.R")
```

## Prepare
```{r, warning=F}
df_KLEMS<-
  KLEMS_growth_raw%>%
  # delete first column
  select(-V1)%>%
  # spread var to manipulate the columns
  spread(key=var,value=value)%>%
  # delete variables that are also in national accounts
  select(-VA_CP,-VA_PYP,-VA_Q)%>%
  left_join(KLEMS_NA_raw,by=c("year","geo_code","geo_name","nace_r2_code","nace_r2_name"))%>%
  # select the relevant variables: TFP, GO_PI, GO_Q
  # Factor shares
  # Labour
  mutate(share_L_GO=LAB/GO_CP,
         # II share of GO
         share_II_GO=II_CP/GO_CP)%>%
  # Capital share of GO
  mutate(share_K_GO=1-share_L_GO-share_II_GO)%>%
  # ln(X(t+1))-ln(X(t))%>%
  group_by(geo_code,nace_r2_code)%>%
  mutate(log_change_GO=log(GO_Q)-log(lag(GO_Q)),
         log_change_L=log(LAB_QI)-log(lag(LAB_QI)),
         log_change_II=log(II_Q)-log(lag(II_Q)),
         log_change_VA_PI=log(VA_PI)-log(lag(VA_PI)),
         log_change_K=log(CAP_QI)-log(lag(CAP_QI)))%>%
  mutate(log_change_TFP_GO=
           log_change_GO -
           log_change_L*lag(share_L_GO)-
           log_change_II*lag(share_II_GO)-
           log_change_K*lag(share_K_GO))%>%
  select(geo_code,geo_name,nace_r2_code,nace_r2_name,year,log_change_TFP_GO,VA_PI,GO_PI,GO_Q,log_change_VA_PI)%>%
  rename("Aihat"="log_change_TFP_GO","pi"="GO_PI","yi"="GO_Q",
         "va_pi"="VA_PI",
         "vapihat"="log_change_VA_PI",
         "country"="geo_code",
         "sector"="nace_r2_code",
         "country_name"="geo_name",
         "sector_name"="nace_r2_name",
         "Year"="year")%>%
  filter(!is.na(Aihat) & !is.na(pi) & !is.na(yi))%>%
  mutate(yi=ifelse(is.infinite(yi)|yi==0,NA,yi),
         pi=ifelse(is.infinite(pi)|pi==0,NA,pi))%>%
  mutate(si=yi*pi)%>%
  arrange(country,sector,Year)%>%
  mutate(ratio_change_x = exp(Aihat), # Convert log changes back to ratio
         Ai = 100 * cumprod(ratio_change_x))%>%
  # Cleaning outliers
   filter(!country %in% c("SK","IE","EL","EU11","EU12"))%>%
  filter(!sector %in% c("MARKT"    ,"MARKTxAG","TOT","T","TOT_IND"))%>%
  left_join(GDP_deflator,by=c("country"="geo_code","Year"="year"))
  
sales<-
  df_KLEMS%>%
    group_by(country,Year)%>%
    summarise(s=sum(pi*yi))


df_KLEMS<-
  df_KLEMS%>%
  left_join(sales,by=c("country","Year"))

```

Functions
```{r,warning=F}
# Define the function to calculate growth rates for a given n
calculate_growth <- function(df, n) {
  df %>%
    group_by(sector, country) %>%
    mutate(n_sector=row_number(Year))%>%
    mutate(
      Aihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(Ai) - log(lag(Ai, n)), NA_real_),
      pihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(pi) - log(lag(pi, n)), NA_real_),
      yihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(yi) - log(lag(yi, n)), NA_real_),
      sihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(si) - log(lag(si, n)), NA_real_),
      shat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(s) - log(lag(s, n)), NA_real_),
      hat_infl = if_else(n_sector > n, log(gdp_deflator) - log(lag(gdp_deflator, n)), NA_real_),
      horizon = n  # Add the horizon column indicating the value of n
    ) %>%
    # Ensure to select new columns including the horizon column
    select(Year, country, sector, sector_name, Aihat, pihat, yihat,sihat,shat,hat_infl, horizon, pi, yi,si,s) %>%
    ungroup()
}
```

```{r,warning=F}
  mutate(yi = ifelse(is.infinite(yi) | yi == 0, NA, yi),
         pi = ifelse(is.infinite(pi) | pi == 0, NA, pi))

# Specify the range of n (long term growth rate from t to t+n)
n_values <- 1:25  #

# Apply the function for each n and combine the results
df_KLEMS_growth_rate <- map_dfr(n_values, ~calculate_growth(df_KLEMS_prepared, .x))
df_KLEMS_growth_rate<-df_KLEMS_growth_rate%>%filter(!is.na(Aihat) & !is.na(hat_infl))
```

## Distribution of zeta

Computing $\zeta$ for each country and each time horizon (1, that is year on year growth rate) or long term growth rate (between $t$ and $t+\tau$.)

\[
\zeta_{i,t,t+1}=\frac{\hat{A}_{i,t,1}+\hat{p}_{i,t,1}}{\hat{X}_{i,t,1}+\hat{p}_{i,t,1}}.
\]

\[
\zeta_{i,t,\tau}=\frac{\hat{A}_{i,t,\tau}+\hat{p}_{i,t,\tau}}{\hat{X}_{i,t,\tau}+\hat{p}_{i,t,t+\tau}}.
\]


```{r,fig.width=4,fig.height=4}
computed_zeta_KLEMS<-
  df_KLEMS_growth_rate%>%
  mutate(computed_zeta=(Aihat+(pihat-hat_infl))/(pihat-hat_infl+yihat))%>%
  select(country,sector,Year,horizon,computed_zeta)

g_density_zeta_KLEMS<-
  computed_zeta_KLEMS%>%
  ggplot()+
  geom_density(aes(x=computed_zeta),fill="#CCFFCC")+
  mytheme+
   labs(y="Density",x = expression("Computed " * zeta),
       caption="KLEMS, all growth rates pooled")+
  xlim(-5,5)
g_density_zeta_KLEMS
save_graph("g_density_zeta_KLEMS",width=4,height=4)
```


```{r}
g_density_zeta_KLEMS_horizon<-
  computed_zeta_KLEMS%>%
  mutate(horizon_factor=factor(horizon,levels=seq(60,1)))%>%
  ggplot()+
  geom_density_ridges(aes(x=computed_zeta,y=horizon_factor),fill="#CCFFCC")+
  mytheme+
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size=8))+
  labs(y="Horizon",x = expression("Computed " * zeta),
       caption="KLEMS, long term growth rates")+
  xlim(-5,5)

g_density_zeta_KLEMS_horizon
save_graph("g_density_zeta_KLEMS_horizon",width=4,height=6)
```

## Optimisation

Minimising the mean absolute error between the predicted industry-level productivity growth and the real productivity.

```{r,warning=F}
df<-df_KLEMS_growth_rate%>%
                 filter(horizon>=15)

result_KLEMS<- optimize(compute_mean_abs_error, lower = 0, upper = 1) # Adjust the interval as needed
result_KLEMS$minimum # The value that minimizes the function
# result_KLEMS$objective # The minimized value of the function
```

### Plots

Prediction error of productivity growth between t and t+horizon

For each horizon $t+\tau$, we plot 

\[    \text{Mean error}_{t,t+\tau}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i,t}(\hat{A}^{\text{pred}}_{i,t,\tau}-\hat{A}_{i,t,\tau})\]




Plotting the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and the Root Mean Square error (RMSE)

\[    \text{Mean Absolute Error (MAE)}_{t,t+\tau}=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i,t}| \hat{A}^{\text{pred}}_{i,t,\tau}-\hat{A}_{i,t,\tau}|\]

\[    \text{Root Mean Square error (RMSE)}_{t,t+\tau}=\sqrt{\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i,t} (\hat{A}^{\text{pred}}_{i,t,\tau}-\hat{A}_{i,t,\tau})^2}\]


- How strong exactly is the argument that long horizon error distributions are much more poorly estimated? A simple diagnostic is the number of points in a distribution as a function of horizon.

```{r}
build_error_distribution_counts <- function(df_growth_rate, best_zeta, db_name) {
  counts <- df_growth_rate %>%
    mutate(
      predAihat = best_zeta * yihat + (best_zeta - 1) * (pihat - hat_infl),
      error = Aihat - predAihat
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(error), is.finite(error)) %>%
    group_by(horizon) %>%
    summarise(
      n_error_points = n(),
      n_countries = n_distinct(country),
      n_sectors = n_distinct(sector),
      n_country_sector_pairs = n_distinct(country, sector),
      n_start_years = n_distinct(Year - horizon),
      n_end_years = n_distinct(Year),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    arrange(horizon)

  if (nrow(counts) == 0) {
    return(tibble(
      db = db_name,
      horizon = numeric(),
      n_error_points = integer(),
      n_countries = integer(),
      n_sectors = integer(),
      n_country_sector_pairs = integer(),
      n_start_years = integer(),
      n_end_years = integer(),
      n_error_points_h1 = integer(),
      share_of_h1 = numeric()
    ))
  }

  h1_count <- counts$n_error_points[counts$horizon == min(counts$horizon, na.rm = TRUE)][1]

  counts %>%
    mutate(
      db = db_name,
      n_error_points_h1 = h1_count,
      share_of_h1 = n_error_points / n_error_points_h1
    ) %>%
    select(db, everything())
}

df_error_distribution_counts_KLEMS <-
  build_error_distribution_counts(df_KLEMS_growth_rate, best_zeta_mae_KLEMS, "KLEMS")

df_error_distribution_counts_KLEMS_summary <-
  df_error_distribution_counts_KLEMS %>%
  summarise(
    n_h1 = first(n_error_points),
    n_h15 = n_error_points[match(15, horizon)],
    share_h15_vs_h1 = n_error_points[match(15, horizon)] / first(n_error_points),
    horizon_last = max(horizon, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_last = last(n_error_points),
    share_last_vs_h1 = last(share_of_h1)
  )

write_excel_csv(
  df_error_distribution_counts_KLEMS,
  file = file.path(tables_path, "tab_error_distribution_points_by_horizon_KLEMS.csv")
)
write_excel_csv(
  df_error_distribution_counts_KLEMS_summary,
  file = file.path(tables_path, "tab_error_distribution_points_by_horizon_KLEMS_summary.csv")
)
```

The maximum horizon available as a time series is 24 years, and we need error at horizon 30 (From 2022 to 2050). Because the number of error draws falls sharply after $\tau=20$, the main confidence-band specification estimates empirical error distributions up to $\tau=20$ and linearly extrapolates the distribution moments from there.

Function
```{r}
# Define a function to fit a linear model and predict new values
predict_new_horizons <- function(df, horizon_extend) {
  # Fit a linear model
  df_filtered <- df %>% filter(horizon > max(horizon) - 10)
  model <- lm(value ~ horizon, data = df_filtered)
  # Create a new dataframe for prediction
  new_data <- tibble(horizon = (max(df$horizon) + 1):horizon_extend)
  # Predict values for new horizons
  predictions <- predict(model, newdata = new_data)
  # Return the new data with predictions
  return(new_data %>%
           mutate(predicted_value = predictions))
}
```



```{r}
# Extend the horizon for each quantile column
horizon_extend <- 30

df_quantiles_error<-read_csv(file= file.path(dataset_path, "quantiles_KLEMS.csv"))

df_quantiles_error_empirical <-
  df_quantiles_error %>%
  filter(horizon <= error_distribution_empirical_cutoff)

extended_df <- df_quantiles_error_empirical %>%
  pivot_longer(-horizon, names_to = "quantile", values_to = "value") %>%
  group_by(quantile) %>%
  do(predict_new_horizons(., horizon_extend)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(is_extrapolated = TRUE)

# See the extended dataframe
print(extended_df)

g_quantile_extension_KLEMS_tau20 <-
ggplot(extended_df,aes(x=horizon,y=predicted_value,colour=quantile,group=quantile))+
  geom_line(aes(linetype="Extended"))+
  geom_line(data=df_quantiles_error_empirical%>%
              gather(key=quantile,value=predicted_value,-1),aes(linetype="Past data"))+
  geom_vline(xintercept = error_distribution_empirical_cutoff, linetype = 2)+
  scale_linetype_manual(values=c("Past data"=1,"Extended"=2))+
  mytheme+
  theme(legend.box="vertical")+
  labs(colour="Quantiles",linetype="",title="KLEMS confidence interval and extension beyond 20Y")
g_quantile_extension_KLEMS_tau20
save_graph("g_quantile_extension_KLEMS_tau20", width = 8, height = 4)
```

```{r,fig.height=10,fig.width=15}
         q90_aihat=predAihat+q90)%>%
```

## Robustness checks

```{r}
df<-
  df_KLEMS_growth_rate%>%
                 filter(horizon>=15)
```




### Absolute mean error

Minimisation of the absolute mean error

```{r,warning=F}


result_KLEMS<- optimize(compute_abs_mean_error, lower = 0, upper = 1) # Adjust the interval as needed
cat("Zeta \n")
result_KLEMS$minimum # The value that minimizes the function
cat("Objective value\n")
result_KLEMS$objective # The minimized value of the function
```

### Mean absolute error

Minimisation of the mean absolute error

```{r,warning=F}


 
result_KLEMS<- optimize(compute_mean_abs_error, lower = 0, upper = 1) # Adjust the interval as needed
cat("Zeta \n")
result_KLEMS$minimum # The value that minimizes the function
cat("Objective value\n")
result_KLEMS$objective # The minimized value of the function
```


### Mean error

Minimisation of the mean error. 

Note that to make sure the error is the closest to 0 (and not as negative as possible), we optimise for the absolute value of the mean error to be equal to 0. De facto, the result is equivalent to optimising the absolute mean error.

```{r,warning=F}



result_KLEMS<- optimize(compute_mean_error, lower = 0, upper = 1) # Adjust the interval as needed
cat("Zeta \n")
result_KLEMS$minimum # The value that minimizes the function
cat("Objective value\n")
result_KLEMS$objective # The minimized value of the function
```
### Median error



Minimisation of the absolute median error. 

```{r,warning=F}


result_KLEMS<- optimize(compute_median_error, lower = 0, upper = 1) # Adjust the interval as needed
cat("Zeta \n")
result_KLEMS$minimum # The value that minimizes the function
cat("Objective value\n")
result_KLEMS$objective # The minimized value of the function
```
### Median Absolute error


Minimisation of the  median absolute error. 

```{r,warning=F}

result_KLEMS$objective # The minimized value of the function
```

### Root mean square error

Minimisation of the root mean square error

```{r,warning=F}

cat("Objective value\n")
result_KLEMS$objective # The minimized value of the function
```

### Sales weighted optimisation


In the previous section, each sector is treated equally, as a result, services sectors, more numerous (and also representing a highest share of developped economies' GDP) are over-represented. 

As a robustness check, we adapt the optimisation technique to give each sector a weight proportional to its sales. it then over-represents higher income countries and higher output sectors. 

As a second robustness check, we also weight by the output share of each sector. Thus, each country is represented equally, but within it, each sector is weighted by it's respective output share. 


```{r}



result_KLEMS_sales_weighted<- optimize(compute_mean_error_sales_weighted, lower = 0, upper = 1) # Adjust the interval as needed
cat("Zeta \n")
result_KLEMS_sales_weighted$minimum # The value that minimizes the function
cat("Objective value\n")
result_KLEMS_sales_weighted$objective # The minimized value of the function
```



```{r}

result_KLEMS_sales_share_weighted<- optimize(compute_mean_error_sales_share_weighted, lower = 0, upper = 1) # Adjust the interval as needed
cat("Zeta \n")
result_KLEMS_sales_share_weighted$minimum # The value that minimizes the function
cat("Objective value\n")
result_KLEMS_sales_share_weighted$objective # The minimized value of the function
```

Functions
```{r,warning=F}
# Define the function to calculate growth rates for a given n
calculate_growth <- function(df, n) {
  df %>%
    group_by(sector, country) %>%
    mutate(n_sector=row_number(Year))%>%
    mutate(
      Aihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(Ai) - log(lag(Ai, n)), NA_real_),
      pihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(pi) - log(lag(pi, n)), NA_real_),
      yihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(yi) - log(lag(yi, n)), NA_real_), #GO_hat
     Lihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(L_Q) - log(lag(L_Q, n)), NA_real_), #L
       Kihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(K_Q) - log(lag(K_Q, n)), NA_real_), #Q
      IIihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(II_Q) - log(lag(II_Q, n)), NA_real_), #Q
      meanalpha_L = if_else(n_sector > n, 1/2*(share_L_GO+  lag(share_L_GO, n)), NA_real_), #alpha_L
       meanalpha_K = if_else(n_sector > n, 1/2*(share_K_GO+  lag(share_K_GO, n)), NA_real_), #alpha_K
      meanalpha_II = if_else(n_sector > n, 1/2*(share_II_GO+ lag(share_II_GO, n)), NA_real_), #alpha_II
      lagalpha_L = if_else(n_sector > n, (lag(share_L_GO, n)), NA_real_), #alpha_L
       lagalpha_K = if_else(n_sector > n, (lag(share_K_GO, n)), NA_real_), #alpha_K
      lagalpha_II = if_else(n_sector > n, (lag(share_II_GO, n)), NA_real_), #alpha_II
      hat_infl = if_else(n_sector > n, log(gdp_va_pi) - log(lag(gdp_va_pi, n)), NA_real_),
      horizon = n  # Add the horizon column indicating the value of n
    ) %>%
    # Ensure to select new columns including the horizon column
    select(Year, country, sector, sector_name, Aihat, pihat, yihat,hat_infl,Lihat,
           Kihat,IIihat,meanalpha_L,meanalpha_K, meanalpha_II,
           lagalpha_L,lagalpha_K ,lagalpha_II, horizon, pi, yi,si,s) %>%
    ungroup()
}
```


```{r,warning=F}
# Initial data preparation, getting rid of NA
df_STAN_GO_prepared <- df_STAN_GO %>%
  filter(!is.na(Ai) & !is.na(pi) & !is.na(yi) & !is.na(gdp_va_pi)) %>%
  mutate(yi = ifelse(is.infinite(yi) | yi == 0, NA, yi),
         pi = ifelse(is.infinite(pi) | pi == 0, NA, pi))

# Range of n values
n_values <- 1:10

# Apply the function for each n and combine the results
df_STAN_growthrate <- map_dfr(n_values, ~calculate_growth(df_STAN_GO_prepared, .x))
df_STAN_growthrate<-df_STAN_growthrate%>%filter(!is.na(Aihat) & !is.na(hat_infl))

   mutate(computed_aihat_bis=yihat-Lihat*lagalpha_L-Kihat*lagalpha_K-IIihat*lagalpha_II)%>%
  mutate(gap=computed_aihat-Aihat,

select(Year,country,sector,Aihat,computed_aihat,gap,gap_bis)%>%
```

##Optimise

Minimisation of the mean absolute error

```{r,warning=F}

lim_down <- 0.05
lim_up <- 0.95

df_STAN_calibration_trimmed <-
  df_STAN_growthrate %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  drop_na(Aihat, pihat, yihat, hat_infl) %>%
  filter(is.finite(Aihat), is.finite(pihat), is.finite(yihat), is.finite(hat_infl)) %>%
  filter(Aihat > quantile(Aihat, lim_down) & Aihat < quantile(Aihat, lim_up)) %>%
  filter(pihat > quantile(pihat, lim_down) & pihat < quantile(pihat, lim_up)) %>%
  filter(yihat > quantile(yihat, lim_down) & yihat < quantile(yihat, lim_up)) %>%
  filter(hat_infl > quantile(hat_infl, lim_down) & hat_infl < quantile(hat_infl, lim_up))

compute_mean_abs_error_stan <- function(zeta) {
  predAihat <- zeta * df_STAN_calibration_trimmed$yihat +
    (zeta - 1) * (df_STAN_calibration_trimmed$pihat - df_STAN_calibration_trimmed$hat_infl)
  mean(abs(predAihat - df_STAN_calibration_trimmed$Aihat))
}

result_stan <- optimize(compute_mean_abs_error_stan, lower = 0, upper = 1)
cat("Zeta\n")
result_stan$minimum # The value that minimizes the function
cat("Objective value\n")
result_stan$objective # The minimized value of the function

best_zeta_mae_stan<-result_stan$minimum
```

```{r,warning=F}
result_stan<- optimize(compute_abs_mean_error, lower = 0, upper = 1) # Adjust the interval as needed
result_stan$minimum # The value that minimizes the function
result_stan$objective # The minimized value of the function
```

```{r}
# Define the function to calculate growth rates for a given n
calculate_growth <- function(df, n) {
  df %>%
    group_by(sector, country) %>%
    mutate(n_sector=row_number(Year))%>%
    mutate(
      Aihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(Ai) - log(lag(Ai, n)), NA_real_),
      pihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(pi) - log(lag(pi, n)), NA_real_),
      hat_infl = if_else(n_sector > n, log(GDP_price_index) - log(lag(GDP_price_index, n)), NA_real_),
      yihat = if_else(n_sector > n, log(yi) - log(lag(yi, n)), NA_real_),
      horizon = n  # Add the horizon column indicating the value of n
    ) %>%
    # Ensure to select new columns including the horizon column
    select(Year, country, sector, sector_name, Aihat, pihat, yihat, horizon, pi, yi,hat_infl) %>%
    ungroup()
}

# Initial data preparation steps remain the same
df_prepared <- df_nber_raw %>%
  rename(Ai = "tfp5", pi = "piship", yi = "real_output",
         sector = "naics", Year = "year", sector_name = "naics_name") %>%
  mutate(country = "US", country_name = "US") %>%
  filter(!is.na(Ai) & !is.na(pi) & !is.na(yi) & !is.na(GDP_price_index)) %>%
  mutate(yi = ifelse(is.infinite(yi) | yi == 0, NA, yi),
         pi = ifelse(is.infinite(pi) | pi == 0, NA, pi),
         GDP_price_index = ifelse(is.infinite(GDP_price_index) | GDP_price_index == 0, NA, GDP_price_index))

# Specify the range of n values you are interested in
n_values <- 1:60  # For example, from 1 to 5 years

# Apply the function for each n and combine the results
df_nber_growthrate <- map_dfr(n_values, ~calculate_growth(df_prepared, .x))
df_nber_growthrate<-df_nber_growthrate%>%filter(!is.na(Aihat))
```

```{r}
# Paper version (SI Table S4): same numbers, grouped by metric family. A float
# rather than a longtable, which overflowed the SI page it shares with Fig. S4.
zeta_s4_row <- function(error_name, label) {
  r <- df_error_3db %>% filter(Error == error_name)
  vals <- c(r[["Zeta (KLEMS)"]], r[["Zeta (KLEMS, horizon $\\geq$ 15)"]],
            r[["Zeta (KLEMS, $15\\leq$ horizon $\\leq$ 20)"]], r[["Zeta (STAN)"]],
            r[["Zeta (NBER CES)"]])
  paste0(label, " & ", paste(sprintf("%.3f", vals), collapse = " & "), " \\\\")
}
zeta_s4_group <- function(title) {
  c(paste0("\\multicolumn{6}{l}{\\textit{", title, "}}\\\\"), "\\addlinespace")
}
```

```{r}
make_zeta_calibration_row <- function(dataset, sample, df_sample) {
  df_calibration <- df_sample %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    drop_na(Aihat, yihat, pihat, hat_infl) %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(Aihat),
      is.finite(yihat),
      is.finite(pihat),
      is.finite(hat_infl)
    )

  mae_objective <- function(zeta) {
    predAihat <- zeta * df_calibration$yihat +
      (zeta - 1) * (df_calibration$pihat - df_calibration$hat_infl)
    mean(abs(predAihat - df_calibration$Aihat))
  }

  result <- optimize(mae_objective, lower = 0, upper = 1)

  tibble(
    Dataset = dataset,
    Sample = sample,
    Horizons = paste0(min(df_calibration$horizon), "--", max(df_calibration$horizon)),
    Observations = nrow(df_calibration),
    zeta_mae = result$minimum
  )
}

df_STAN_calibration_trimmed <-

  filter(is.finite(Aihat), is.finite(pihat), is.finite(yihat), is.finite(hat_infl)) %>%
  filter(Aihat > quantile(Aihat, lim_down) & Aihat < quantile(Aihat, lim_up)) %>%
  filter(pihat > quantile(pihat, lim_down) & pihat < quantile(pihat, lim_up)) %>%
  filter(yihat > quantile(yihat, lim_down) & yihat < quantile(yihat, lim_up)) %>%
  filter(hat_infl > quantile(hat_infl, lim_down) & hat_infl < quantile(hat_infl, lim_up))
```

Robustness: nonoverlapping KLEMS industries (Appendix A6, data construction)

The baseline pools NACE sections with their subdivisions (e.g. C with C10-C12, G with G45-G47), so some industries enter at more than one level of aggregation. Here we keep only the finest nonoverlapping partition: subdivisions where KLEMS reports them, sections otherwise. Combined codes (C20-C21, C26-C27, D-E, M-N, O-Q, R-S) and sections with reported subdivisions (C, G, H, J, Q) are dropped.

```{r}
summarise_forecast_error_by_horizon <- function(df_sample, best_zeta, db_name) {
  df_sample %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    drop_na(Aihat, pihat, yihat, hat_infl) %>%
    filter(is.finite(Aihat), is.finite(pihat), is.finite(yihat), is.finite(hat_infl)) %>%
    mutate(
      predAihat = best_zeta * yihat + (best_zeta - 1) * (pihat - hat_infl),
      error = predAihat - Aihat
    ) %>%
    group_by(horizon) %>%
    summarise(
      MAE = mean(abs(error)),
      RMSE = sqrt(mean(error^2)),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    pivot_longer(c(MAE, RMSE), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(db = db_name)
}

df_error_metrics_by_dataset <-

    summarise_forecast_error_by_horizon(
      df_KLEMS_growth_rate,
      best_zeta_mae_KLEMS,

    ),
    summarise_forecast_error_by_horizon(
      df_nber_clean,
      best_zeta_mae_nber,
      "NBER CES"
    ),
    summarise_forecast_error_by_horizon(
      df_STAN_calibration_trimmed,
      best_zeta_mae_stan,
      "STAN"
    )
  )

common_horizon_max <-

  group_by(db) %>%
  summarise(max_horizon = max(horizon, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  summarise(common_horizon_max = min(max_horizon, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  pull(common_horizon_max)

  "STAN" = paste0("STAN (zeta=", sprintf("%.2f", best_zeta_mae_stan), ")")
)
```
